subject: Slate stability — request for close buffer and MAP alignment
messages:
From: Jordan Matthews <jordan@talosbio.io>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, procurement@talosbio.io
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance window pressure + proposed SOW tweak

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

Quick update from our side — procurement surfaced a vendor review that will push our signature by ~10 business days if we don't surface a narrower SOW for immediate internal review. TL;DR: the eval team needs a smaller acceptance slice to run the initial integration tests (we can do the rest post-acceptance).

We'd like to ask for a modest buffer on the close date so we don't force a rushed cutover that would break the eval cadence. I attached a trimmed SOW (Talos_SOW_v2.pdf) with two deliverables moved to post-acceptance.

Can Redwood update the MAP to reflect a partial acceptance milestone and a 10-business-day buffer? If we can get that documented we can keep the internal calendar in sync and avoid an escalation.

Proposed next steps:
- PRIO: Redwood countersigned MAP update that includes a partial acceptance milestone (by EOD Fri if possible)
- Talos: procurement will complete their compliance checklist within the buffer window
- Both: short call Monday to confirm test plan (30 min)

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan Matthews
Head of Platforms, Talos Bio
jordan@talosbio.io
Attachments: Talos_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 412 KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan@talosbio.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance window pressure + proposed SOW tweak

Jordan — thanks for the heads-up and for the trimmed SOW. I reviewed Talos_SOW_v2.pdf and the proposed de-scope for initial acceptance makes sense operationally. We can accommodate a partial-acceptance milestone in the MAP and add a 10-business-day schedule buffer to the close gate.

Operational asks from our side:
- Please confirm the exact acceptance criteria you want gated into the partial milestone (test corpus, throughput threshold, and one cross-region query).
- If procurement needs proof-of-dataflow for compliance, tell me which artifacts they require; we can produce a limited audit bundle rather than the full logs set.

I've attached a quick MAP-diff spreadsheet that shows the minimal edits I propose (MAP-diff-20250925.xlsx). If Marissa/Stephanie are good with the language, I can send a formal MAP update and DocuSign link by EOD Friday.

Proposed meeting: Mon 9/29 10:00am PT for the integration test plan (30m).

Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Sep 2025 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acceptance window pressure + proposed SOW tweak

Priyom / Steph — quick internal note (mirroring Jordan's ask).

Summary of risk: procurement hold -> likely signature slip of ~10 business days; primary risk is calendar drift that impacts our planned canary acceptance dates and billing start. If we let the customer proceed with a partial-accept milestone + 10-business-day buffer, we:
- Reduce churn risk by keeping momentum on integration tests
- Preserve billing cadence if we gate final invoicing on full acceptance
- Increase operational complexity slightly (two-stage acceptance + short canary)

Mitigation proposal (my recommendation):
- Approve the partial-accept milestone for the MAP with explicit pass/fail criteria (list test corpus + perf threshold + one cross-region test)
- Create a short-run canary (week-long, single shard) that gives Talos confidence and lets us validate infra + observability before full roll
- Delay billing to final acceptance; offer a short credit to cover extended evaluation days if they request (we can authorize up to $3k without exec sign-off)

If Steph or I push the MAP update, I want the language to include clear rollback conditions and an automatic escalation if the canary fails. Priyom — if you can draft the update language I will review and route.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acceptance window pressure + proposed SOW tweak

Thanks for the summary — agree with Marissa's mitigation path. Quick decisions from leadership:

1) APPROVE: 10 business day buffer + partial-accept milestone in the MAP. Language must include the three acceptance criteria (test corpus, throughput >= 95% baseline, one cross-region query success).
2) Operational constraints: run a one-week canary on a single shard before final roll; if the canary fails we will automatically pause the roll and open a SOC/ops postmortem.
3) Billing: delay invoicing to final acceptance; offer a one-time evaluation credit up to $2,500 if Talos requests. Any credit >$2,500 requires a VP sign-off.

Priyom — please finalize the MAP edits and send the DocuSign link to Jordan and procurement. Also include a short table in the MAP that enumerates the rollback conditions and expected telemetry (error rate, p99 latencies, token throughput).

Related links: HubSpot deal HS-78291 (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-78291). I want procurement to get a DocuSign with the partial-accept language (https://www.docusign.com/sign/TALOS-INVITE).

I'll cc Legal only if Talos requests additional SLA exceptions.
